title: Round 2 - eight regimes, a metric that can see insurance, and a promotion rule that cannot count
focus: Does widening the window matrix to eight regimes, adding a genuine crash quarter and two directionless chop windows, change the ranking, and does a dominance view (median, worst window, hit rate, Pareto frontier) fix the median-only metric's blindness to hedge and convex payoffs that round 1 exposed?
headline: The programme's own two-consecutive-rounds promotion rule does not survive contact with a deterministic engine: re-scoring a frozen card on an old window in a later round recomputes the identical number rather than sampling anything new.
outcome:
Twenty-seven cards, round 1's twenty-two carried forward unchanged plus five new challengers, traded across eight market regimes. Re-running a round-1 card on a round-1 window in round 2 reproduced the identical figure on twenty of twenty checked pairs, verified bit-identical, which means a promotion rule requiring a positive median in two consecutive rounds counts one measurement twice unless the second round brings genuinely new windows.

The dominance view earned its place: c09-convex, designed to test whether it was worth adding, reached the Pareto frontier at 4th of 22 by Borda composite, where round 1's median-only rule would have placed it 11th.

But decomposing the GFC window showed capital exposure correlates strongly and positively with adjusted excess in a falling market, because the adjustment credits exposure proportional to a negative benchmark - so per unit of capital actually deployed, the ordering in that window inverts.

The two new chop windows mostly re-measured variance the matrix already carried, and the single most redundant pair in the whole eight-window matrix was not a chop pair at all but q4-2018 and bear-2022.

Applying the promotion rule mechanically would have replaced B-momentum with B2-hold-90 on margins comfortably inside the ordering noise floor the same protocol document calls meaningless - no such promotion was made, and the rule was flagged for amendment.

A third engine defect, a concurrent read colliding with the tournament's write lock, recurred during round 2's own setup and cost an entire first attempt: 135 card-runs, zero results, from a run that survived being killed by taskkill.
carries_forward: The two-consecutive-rounds promotion rule needs amendment, since re-scoring frozen cards on old windows double-counts a single measurement rather than confirming it.
Capital exposure correlates strongly with adjusted excess in falling markets, so per-unit-of-capital comparisons should be checked separately from the raw ranking in crash windows.
The chop windows added this round are largely redundant with existing bear windows and should not be assumed to add independent regime coverage.
A third engine defect (concurrent-read lock collision) was found; future rounds should refuse to start while another tournament process is alive.
